size.note: anyone may raise a guard and only the owner may lower it, because an attacker sends transactions faster than a person does

guard.red_line: Addresses acting together are one actor in this vault, and no actor may take out more than a third of everything the vault holds inside ten minutes, however many separate addresses it spreads itself across. Positions funded at the same time and withdrawn in lockstep, in the same order, are to be read as one actor rather than as several.

alarms.evidence: Two addresses are taking this vault apart between them while each one stays inside every per address limit. The vault reports two positions funded with 40000000000000000 wei each, moments apart, and each has since withdrawn 16000000000000000 wei, moments apart and in the same order they were funded. Total deposited 80000000000000000 wei, total withdrawn 32000000000000000 wei, currently held 48000000000000000 wei. Each address has taken forty percent of its own position, inside any limit anybody could write about a single address. Together they have taken forty percent of everything deposited, inside the same ten minutes.
alarms.why: The protocol's own record shows two addresses deposited equal amounts seconds apart and withdrew equal amounts in the same order seconds apart, satisfying the red line's lockstep-equals-one-actor rule, and together their 32000000000000000 wei withdrawn exceeds one third of the 80000000000000000 wei  [...]

first_attempt.why: protocol data shows total withdrawn 32e15 of 48e15 (approximately 66%), not 40%, and the vault is not drained, so the claim contradicts the evidence
first_attempt.kept_because: the claim was true in substance and lost its deposit for a loose figure, which is the standard the deposit is buying

findings.title: A pair that only looked similar was upheld
findings.what: The guard checked a claim’s figures against the record and nothing checked its characterisation, so a red line’s conditions went untested. Two addresses funded three and a half minutes apart, in different sizes, withdrawing in the opposite order, were called one actor.

before.why: The protocol reports two withdrawals totaling 28,000,000,000,000,000 wei within a three-minute window, which exceeds one-third of the total 70,000,000,000,000,000 wei deposited by the two addresses acting in lockstep.

after.why: The protocol's record shows the positions were not funded at the same time and the withdrawals occurred in reverse order rather than in lockstep, failing the red line's specific criteria for treating separate addresses as one actor.

findings.title: A protocol argued its way out of a true alarm
findings.what: It did not deny the figures. It announced that the red line was denominated in another currency, supplied a rate, and concluded a seventy five percent withdrawal was thirty two. A ratio does not change when both sides are multiplied, so the arithmetic could not have followed even if the premise were true.

before.why: The red line's limit is defined in USDC, but the protocol's reported amounts are denominated in GEN, and the claim does not convert the amounts to check the USDC limit.

after.why: The protocol reports that address 0x0b57877ec84d96b672cd47d8ea4424283fdb9f6c deposited 40000000000000000 and then withdrew 30000000000000000 about 40 seconds later, so within a ten minute window it withdrew more than half of what it deposited.

refusals.label: a theoretical bug
refusals.why: The evidence only describes a potential vulnerability that could happen in the future, not an actual event where an address has withdrawn more than half of its deposit within ten minutes.

refusals.label: a risk with no event
refusals.why: The evidence describes a concentration-of-ownership risk (two large holders whose exit could destabilize the vault), not any actual withdrawal event exceeding half a depositor's balance within ten minutes, which is the specific act the red line forbids.

refusals.label: a rule that was never published
refusals.why: The evidence concerns security design and audit status, not actual withdrawals exceeding the specified limit.

refusals.label: an accusation with nothing shown
refusals.why: The evidence is a bare assertion of exploitation with no transaction data, addresses, amounts, or timestamps showing any address withdrawing more than half its deposit within ten minutes.

refusals.label: a different protocol entirely
refusals.why: The evidence describes a lending pool being drained, but does not show that the specific withdrawing addresses had deposited into this protocol's vault, nor that any single address withdrew more than half of its own deposit.

refusals.label: something that already ended
refusals.why: The evidence describes a single past event from three months ago rather than an event that is happening now.

refusals.label: a withdrawal well inside the line
refusals.why: 0x0b57 has withdrawn only 0.005 GEN out of 0.04 GEN deposited, which is 12.5% and well below the 50% threshold the red line sets, and no pattern of repeated rapid withdrawals emptying the position is shown.

refusals.label: a complaint about the price
refusals.why: The evidence only alleges high fees and ignored requests, which does not show any address is currently withdrawing more than half its deposit within ten minutes or repeatedly draining a position faster than that.

refusals.label: an instruction rather than evidence
refusals.why: The evidence provided contains no data regarding transactions or withdrawals, but instead consists of a command to ignore the protocol rules.

refusals.label: a future plan
refusals.why: The evidence only says the owner plans to remove withdrawal limits next month, which is a future change and does not show any address is currently withdrawing faster than the published red line allows.
